segments.heading: File comment: checks added for bwx12 (round 5)
segments.text: A line `bwx12+` and the next line `bwx12-` enclose text that was added for bwx12. This comment lists the checks for the 26 kernels of round 5, and what these checks cannot see. Of the six kernels of the whole-chip test, only `read_nop256` belongs to round 5.

segments.heading: File comment: checks added for bwx11 (round 4)
segments.text: The same marking for the text that bwx11 added. Round 4 added three read kernels and the function `test_evict`. One of the three, `read_nop96`, runs in part L of the whole-chip test.

segments.heading: File comment: checks added for bwx10 (round 3)
segments.text: The same marking for the text that bwx10 added. Round 3 added five read kernels and the functions `test_trial_hot` and `test_hot_touch`. One of the five, `read_1pl`, runs in part L of the whole-chip test.

segments.heading: File comment: the base self-test (text written for bwx8)
segments.text:
This is the oldest part of the comment. It names bwx8. It holds for bwx12 in the same way: bwx12.c includes this file [Ref1].
- The self-test and a timed run are one binary. Both reach a kernel through `call` and the table `kernels[]`.
- Each test buffer lies between two PROT_NONE pages. A load or a store up to one page outside the buffer is a fault. The fault ends the process, except in `test_touch` (line 235), which installs a handler.

The checks per kind of kernel, and the limits.
- `oldread` returns a sum. The test compares it with the sum of all words.
- The new read kernel `read` and `asmread` return nothing. For them the test proves that every page of the range is touched. It does not prove that every byte is loaded.
- For the bytes that such a kernel loads, the objdump listing is the evidence [Ref7].

The checks of the trial mode (`test_trial`) and of its output rows (`test_emit`). The whole-chip test does not use the trial mode [Ref6]. So these checks do not cover the function `worker` of bwx12.c, which timed the kernels in the whole-chip test.

segments.heading: Global variables
segments.text: `failures` counts the failed checks. `test_touch` uses `fault_jmp` and `fault_addr`: the place to continue after a fault, and the address of the fault.

segments.heading: Function `guarded`: a buffer between two PROT_NONE pages
segments.text:
- Reserves `n` words (8 bytes each) plus one page before them and one page after them. The whole range is PROT_NONE at first.
- Then it makes the `n` words readable and writable, and returns their address.
- On an error it prints the reason and ends the process with status 2.
- On CRB (page size 4096 B) every caller passes a multiple of the page size. So the last word ends directly before the PROT_NONE page.

segments.heading: Function `unguard`: releases a guarded buffer
segments.text: Unmaps the buffer and its two PROT_NONE pages.

segments.heading: Function `pattern`: test value of one word
segments.text: Returns `(i + 1)` times an odd 64-bit constant, then XOR `salt`. Two different word numbers `i` always give two different values. Two different `salt` values give two different patterns for the same `i`.

segments.heading: Function `calling`: names the kernel before it runs
segments.text: Prints `call,<kernel>,<bytes>`. The output is line-buffered (line 678), so this line is written before the kernel starts. If the kernel ends the process, this line names it.

segments.heading: Function `check`: one result line of a kernel check
segments.text: Prints the kernel name, the name of the check, the bytes, and `pass` or `FAIL`. A failed check adds 1 to `failures`. The self-test continues after it.

segments.heading: Function `is_read`: read kernel or not
segments.text: True for the two read kinds. `T_OLDREAD` is `oldread` and `oldread2`: they return a sum. `oldread2` is a second copy of `oldread`: the same source under another name [Ref1]. `T_READ` is every other read kernel, for example `read` and `asmread`: they return nothing.

segments.heading: Function `test_size`: one kernel on a whole guarded buffer
segments.text:
- Runs the kernel once on a whole guarded buffer. `selftest` passes three sizes: 1 page, 3 pages and 1 MiB.
- **Proves**, every kernel: no load and no store within one page outside its buffers. Such an access ends the process. A prefetch raises no fault, so the check does not see one.
- **Proves**, read kernel: the buffer is unchanged after the call.
- **Proves**, old read kernel: the returned sum equals the sum of all words.
- **Proves**, write and copy kernel: every word of the range holds the right value after the call.
- **Cannot prove**: that `read` or `asmread` load anything. A read kernel without a return value that loads nothing passes here. `test_touch` (line 235) checks a part of this.
Gives every word of `a` its own value and sets `b` to 0. `sum` becomes the sum of all words of `a` in 64-bit arithmetic (an overflow wraps).

Prints the `call` line. Then runs the kernel on the whole buffer (offset 0, `n * 8` bytes) through `call` of bwx12.c.
- `call` chooses the arguments by the kind. A read kernel gets `a`.
- A write kernel gets `a` and the value `v`, which it stores in every word.
- A copy kernel reads `a` and writes `b`.
- The sum that an old read kernel returns goes to `sink`.

- Read kernel: every word of `a` must still hold its pattern value.
- Kind `T_OLDREAD` in addition: the sum in `sink` must equal `sum`. A kernel that skips one word, or adds one word twice, returns another sum.
Write kernel: every word of `a` must hold `v`. A word that the kernel did not store keeps its pattern value, and no pattern value equals `v`. So a missing store fails the check.
Copy kernel: every word of `b` must hold the pattern value of `a`. `b` held 0 before the call. Then every word of `a` must be unchanged. These are two result lines.
Releases both buffers.

segments.heading: Function `test_block`: 256 B at a page start or end
segments.text:
- Runs the kernel on one block of 256 B (32 words) inside a buffer of one page. 256 B is the smallest range that a kernel may get.
- `off` = 0: the block starts directly after the PROT_NONE page before the buffer. The other value of `off`: the block ends directly before the PROT_NONE page after the buffer.
- **Proves**, every kernel: no load and no store up to one page before the block start (first case), and none up to one page after the block end (second case). Such an access ends the process.
- **Proves**, write and copy kernel: every word of the page outside the block keeps its value.
- **Cannot prove**: which bytes inside the 256 B a read kernel loads. The sum that an old read kernel returns is not compared here.
Fills the page of `a` and the page of `b` with two different patterns. Then runs the kernel on 256 B (`m * 8`) at byte offset `off * 8`.

- Read kernel: every word of the page of `a` must be unchanged.
- Write kernel: the 32 words of the block must hold `v`. Every other word of the page must keep its pattern value.
- Copy kernel: in `b` the 32 words of the block must hold the values of `a`. Every other word of `b` must keep its own pattern value. `a` must be unchanged.
- The name of the check says `page start` for `off` = 0 and `page end` for the other value.
Releases both buffers.

segments.heading: Function `on_fault`: SIGSEGV handler of `test_touch`
segments.text: Stores the address of the faulting access in `fault_addr`. Then it jumps back to the `sigsetjmp` call of line 252, which now returns 1. The kernel call that faulted does not continue.

segments.heading: Function `test_touch`: a read kernel must touch every page
segments.text:
- For read kernels only. The buffer has 3 pages. The loop runs three times. Each time another one of the pages is PROT_NONE, and the kernel runs on the whole buffer.
- The kernel must fault, and the fault address must lie in that page.
- **Proves**: the kernel accesses at least one byte of each of the 3 pages. A kernel that loads nothing, or that leaves out a page, fails.
- **Cannot prove**: that every byte or every 64 B line of a page is loaded. One load per page (4096 B on CRB) passes. The objdump listing is the evidence for the loads [Ref7].
- **Cannot prove**: anything about a nop, a vector add, or the use of a loaded value. They change no memory and raise no fault.
Installs `on_fault` as the handler of SIGSEGV. The flag `SA_SIGINFO` makes Linux pass the fault address to the handler. `old` keeps the setting from before.

- `pg` is the address of page `j`. `mprotect` makes this page PROT_NONE.
- `sigsetjmp` returns 0 at its direct call. So the kernel is called on the whole range of 3 pages.
- When the kernel faults, `on_fault` jumps back to line 252. `sigsetjmp` returns 1 there, and `faulted` becomes 1.
- The argument 1 of `sigsetjmp` saves the signal mask, and the jump restores it. So SIGSEGV can be caught again for the next page.
- Line 256 makes the page readable and writable again.
- `j` and `faulted` are `volatile`: they keep their values across the jump.
The check passes when the kernel faulted and the fault address lies in the PROT_NONE page. The name of the check gives the page number: 0, 1 or 2.
Restores the SIGSEGV setting from before and releases the buffer.

segments.heading: Function `trial_check`: one result line of another check
segments.text: Like `check` (line 134), for a check that belongs to no single kernel. The first field of the line is the word `trial`.

segments.heading: Function `kernel_named`: index of a kernel name
segments.text: Returns the index of the kernel with this name in `kernels[]`. If no kernel has the name, it prints a message and ends the process with status 2.

segments.heading: Function `test_trial`: the records of one trial (trial mode)
segments.text:
- Runs trials on a guarded buffer of 1 MiB through `run_trial` of bwx12.c, the function that the trial mode uses.
- The plan `p`: 1 window of `asmread` (4 ms), 4 prefix windows of `oldread` (2 ms each), 1 window of `read` on 65536 B (3 ms), then 3 target windows of `oldread` (12 ms each). No counters. Bins are on.
- **Proves**: `timed_sequence` writes consistent window records, and the sink check can pass and can fail.
- **Cannot prove**: that the byte count of a window equals the bytes that the kernel read. The checks test multiples, not the number of kernel calls.
- **Cannot prove**: anything about the timing code of the whole-chip test. That code is the function `worker` of bwx12.c (interval mode), and no check of this file runs it [Ref1] [Ref6].

Prepares the worker record `w` as the trial mode needs it: no counter group (`group_fd = -1`), and every word of the buffer holds the same value `w.v`. `run_trial` computes the expected sum of an old read as `w.v` times the number of words.

- First check: the plan gives 9 windows (1 + 4 + 1 + 3), and a target window has room for 3 bins: 1 bin for the 10 ms that end inside the 12 ms, 1 bin for the end of the window, and 1 spare bin.
- `set_windows` of bwx12.c fills the plan fields of the 9 window records.
- `run_trial` runs the 9 windows through `timed_sequence` and then sets `r.sink_ok`.

- `whole`: the window counted more than 0 bytes, and a multiple of its range size.
- `groups`: the bytes are a multiple of 8 MiB (`CHECK_BYTES`). The window loop reads the clock after each 8 MiB.
- `lasts`: end time minus start time is at least the requested duration.
- `order`: the end is later than the start, and the start is not earlier than the end of the window before.
- `bins_ok`, target window: it has 1 to `bin_cap` bins, the last bin holds the bytes and the end time of the window, and time and bytes rise from bin to bin.
- `bins_ok`, other window: it has no bin.
Prints the five results of the loop. Then one more check: `r.sink_ok` is 1. So after a trial that ends with `oldread`, the sink holds the expected sum.

- Second trial, target `read` (the new read kernel): the last old read is now a prefix window. `sink_ok` must still be 1. So the `read` windows after it left the sink unchanged.
- Third trial, prefix `asmread` too: the trial holds no old read. `sink_ok` must be -1, which means not applicable.

Fourth trial: the target is `oldread` again, and line 345 flips one bit of the last word of the buffer. The sum now differs from the expected sum by 1. So `sink_ok` must be 0. This proves that the sink check can fail, and that `oldread` reads the last word of its range.

Checks `first_multiplexed` of bwx12.c on three counter readings that are written here. It must return 1: in target window 1 (the second one, the count starts at 0) the counters ran 50 ns of 100 ns. With equal times it must return -1. Line 354 releases the buffer.

segments.heading: Function `test_trial_hot`: the same checks with `--hot-copy`
segments.text:
- The plan and the window checks of `test_trial`, with `plan.hot_copy = 1`. `run_trial` then calls `timed_sequence_hot` in place of `timed_sequence`.
- `win0` is a second set of the 9 window records. The trial does not use it.
- **Proves**: `timed_sequence_hot` writes consistent window records too, and it leaves the plan fields of each record unchanged.
- **Cannot prove**: anything about the whole-chip test. `--hot-copy` is an option of the trial mode only [Ref1].
Prepares `w` and the buffer as in `test_trial`. Sets `plan.hot_copy`, fills `win` and `win0` from the same plan, and runs the trial on `win`.
`kept`: after the trial, the eight plan fields of each record in `win` equal those in `win0`. The other five flags are the checks of `test_trial` (lines 311 to 325).
Prints the six results and the sink check. Then it flips one bit of the last word and runs the trial again: the sink check must fail. Line 414 sets `plan.hot_copy` back to 0.

segments.heading: Function `on_touch`: SIGSEGV handler of `test_hot_touch`
segments.text:
- `touch_page` is the page that holds the window record. `touch_faults` counts the faults in it.
- A fault inside this page: the handler adds 1 to the count and makes the page readable and writable. After the return the access runs again and succeeds.
- A fault at any other address: the handler sets SIGSEGV back to its default action. After the return the access faults again and ends the process.

segments.heading: `struct toucher` and function `toucher`: the second thread of `test_hot_touch`
segments.text: The data of the second thread: the worker record whose trace it reads, the flag `found`, and two clock values.

- Reads the trace of the worker again and again, for at most 5 s, until it holds the event `EV_KERNEL_FIRST`. The worker writes this event at the first kernel call of a window.
- Then it makes the page of the window record PROT_NONE and reads the clock (`t_none`).
- It sleeps 20 ms, makes the page readable and writable again, and reads the clock (`t_done`).
- If the event does not appear within 5 s, it returns and changes nothing.

segments.heading: Function `hot_touch_run`: one 200 ms window, record page made PROT_NONE
segments.text:
- One trial with a single target window: `asmread` on 1 MiB for 200 ms. No other window, no bins, no counters.
- The window record `win` lies alone in a guarded page. So the page can be made PROT_NONE without an effect on other data.
- `hot` selects the function under test: 0 is `timed_sequence`, 1 is `timed_sequence_hot`.
- Result `faults`: the number of faults in the page of the record.
- Result `inside`: 1 when the PROT_NONE time lay between the start clock read and the end clock read of the window.

Prepares the worker record and the buffer as in `test_trial`. It also allocates a trace (`w.log`). `run_trial` writes events to it, and the second thread reads them. `cur_phase = -1` makes the first kernel call write the event `EV_KERNEL_FIRST`.
Fills the window record and stores its page address for the handler. Installs `on_touch` for SIGSEGV. Sets `plan.hot_copy` to `hot` and prints the `call` line.

- Starts the second thread, runs the trial in this thread, and waits for the second thread.
- Sets `plan.hot_copy` back to 0 and restores the SIGSEGV setting from before.
- `inside` is 1 when the event was found, `t_none` is later than the start clock read of the window, and `t_done` is earlier than its end clock read.
- Releases the trace, the buffer and the page of the record.

segments.heading: Function `test_hot_touch`: `timed_sequence_hot` must not touch the window record
segments.text:
- Runs `hot_touch_run` twice: with `timed_sequence`, then with `timed_sequence_hot`.
- Check 1: in both runs the PROT_NONE time lay inside the window.
- Check 2: `timed_sequence` faulted at least once. It reads the record in every pass. So this run shows that the method can see a touch.
- Check 3: `timed_sequence_hot` did not fault.
- **Proves**: the machine code of `timed_sequence_hot` did not read or write the page of the record while it was PROT_NONE (20 ms).
- **Cannot prove**: the same for the rest of the 200 ms window. Also, the whole-chip test does not use `--hot-copy` [Ref6].

segments.heading: Function `map_lines`: number of memory mappings of the process
segments.text: Counts the lines of `/proc/self/maps`. Linux prints one line per memory mapping of the process in this file. The result is -1 if the file cannot be opened.

segments.heading: Function `test_evict`: the evict step runs and unmaps its memory
segments.text:
- Line 543 calls `map_lines` twice and keeps the second count. The comment gives the reason: the first call lets the C library take its memory for file reading.
- Sets the size to 4 MiB and calls `evict_step` of bwx12.c. That function maps 4 MiB, writes one word per 64 B line in two passes, and unmaps the range.
- **Proves**: the step returns no error, its second clock read is later than its first, and the number of mappings is the same as before.
- **Cannot prove**: that the step removes the benchmark buffer from the caches. No check measures the content of a cache.
- The whole-chip test does not use `--evict-mb` [Ref6].

segments.heading: Function `test_round5`: the 26 new kernels in `kernels[]`
segments.text:
- `want` lists the 26 kernel names of round 5, each with the kind that its name says: 20 read, 4 write, 2 copy.
- **Proves**: each name stands exactly once in `kernels[]` with that kind, and the table has 55 entries.
- Reason: the loop of `selftest` chooses the checks by the kind in `kernels[]`. A wrong kind gives a kernel the wrong checks.
- **Cannot prove**: that the function behind a name holds the instructions that the name says, for example 256 nop in `read_nop256`. The objdump listing is the evidence [Ref7].
- The name check covers no kernel of bwx11 or older. Of the six kernels of the whole-chip test it covers `read_nop256` only.

For each wanted name the loop counts the entries of `kernels[]` with that name and compares their kind. A name that is missing, double or of another kind prints a line that starts with `#`, and the first check fails. The second check compares the number of entries with 55.

segments.heading: Function `has_line`: is a complete line in the text
segments.text: True when `text` holds `line` as a whole line: the match starts at the text start or after a line end, and a line end follows it.

segments.heading: Function `emitted`: the text that `emit_trial` prints
segments.text:
- Opens a stream that writes into memory (`open_memstream`).
- Points the globals `plan.tr` and `rec` to the test plan and the test record. So `emit_trial(w, 0)` of bwx12.c prints trial 0 from them.
- Replaces `stdout` by the memory stream for this one call, and restores it after the call.
- Sets the two globals back to `NULL` and returns the printed text. The caller frees it.

segments.heading: Function `test_emit`: the output rows of one trial
segments.text:
- Writes a trial record by hand: 1 predecessor window, 2 target windows, three counter readings, two page snapshots, CPU times and context-switch counts.
- The record holds three intended defects: no huge-page value in the second snapshot (-1), counters that ran 50 ns of 100 ns in target window 1, and `sink_ok = 0`.
- **Proves**: `emit_trial` prints the values of this record in the right fields of the C, P, E and X rows.
- **Cannot prove**: anything about the rows of the whole-chip csv files. The interval mode prints its rows with other code [Ref1].
- The W rows are printed here, and no check compares them.

Prepares a worker record for `emit_trial`. `group_fd = 0` makes `emit_trial` treat the counter group as open. `cfg.nev = 1` makes `emit_trial` print one event column, and `nev` keeps the old value. Line 652 gets the printed text.

- C rows `C,0,0,100,100,300,5` and `C,0,1,100,50,600,7`: after the trial number and the window number come four differences of two readings: enabled time, running time, thread CPU time (all in ns) and the event count.
- P rows: `pre` holds the first snapshot. `post` holds the second, with `NA` for the missing huge-page value.
- E row `E,0,3400,3000,2,3,100,300,0,read`: wall time 3400 ns, CPU time 3000 ns, 2 voluntary and 3 involuntary context switches, a gap of 100 ns before the first target window, a largest gap of 300 ns, sink check 0, counter state `read`.
- X rows: one row for each of the three defects (`coverage_na`, `count_multiplexed`, `sink`).
- Line 663 frees the text.
Removes the three defects from the record and prints it again. The text must now hold no X row, and the E row must show sink check 1. The last lines free the text and restore `cfg.nev`.

segments.heading: Function `selftest`: entry point of `bwx12 --selftest`
segments.text:
- `main` of bwx12.c calls it for the argument `--selftest` and returns its value as the exit status [Ref1].
- `setvbuf` makes the output line-buffered: each line is written when it is complete. So a kernel that ends the process cannot remove earlier lines.
- The header line gives the page size, the number of kernels, and `aarch64` or `STAND-IN kernels`.
- A page size that is not a multiple of 256 B ends the self-test with the value 2.
- `words`: the three buffer sizes of `test_size`. `offs`: the two block offsets of `test_block`, the first and the last 256 B of a page.
- The whole-chip test calls a kernel on other sizes: 256 MiB for the warm-up, and chunks of 2 MiB in the timed interval [Ref1] [Ref6].

- `test_round5` runs first, before the loop uses the kinds of `kernels[]`.
- The loop takes all 55 kernels in the order of `kernels[]`.
- Per kernel: `test_size` with the three sizes, then `test_block` at the two offsets.
- Per read kernel in addition: `test_touch`.

- Then five checks of the trial mode: `test_trial`, `test_trial_hot`, `test_hot_touch`, `test_evict`, `test_emit`.
- The last line of the output is `# failures=N`.
- Return value: 1 if a check failed, else 0. build12.sh stops with status 4 when the value is not 0 [Ref2].
- For the bwx12 binary of the whole-chip test, the self-test printed 457 `pass` lines, no `FAIL` line and `# failures=0` [Ref3].
